source: DISK II SLOT 6 - I/O AND BOOT0 TARGETS

symbols.name: COMMENT_D2_PH0_OFF
symbols.comment: Disk II slot 6: release stepper phase 0; read or write activates this soft switch. Head movement depends on the phase sequence, not this address alone.

symbols.name: COMMENT_D2_PH0_ON
symbols.comment: Disk II slot 6: energize stepper phase 0; read or write activates this soft switch. Head movement depends on the phase sequence, not this address alone.

symbols.name: COMMENT_D2_PH1_OFF
symbols.comment: Disk II slot 6: release stepper phase 1; read or write activates this soft switch. Head movement depends on the phase sequence, not this address alone.

symbols.name: COMMENT_D2_PH1_ON
symbols.comment: Disk II slot 6: energize stepper phase 1; read or write activates this soft switch. Head movement depends on the phase sequence, not this address alone.

symbols.name: COMMENT_D2_PH2_OFF
symbols.comment: Disk II slot 6: release stepper phase 2; read or write activates this soft switch. Head movement depends on the phase sequence, not this address alone.

symbols.name: COMMENT_D2_PH2_ON
symbols.comment: Disk II slot 6: energize stepper phase 2; read or write activates this soft switch. Head movement depends on the phase sequence, not this address alone.

symbols.name: COMMENT_D2_PH3_OFF
symbols.comment: Disk II slot 6: release stepper phase 3; read or write activates this soft switch. Head movement depends on the phase sequence, not this address alone.

symbols.name: COMMENT_D2_PH3_ON
symbols.comment: Disk II slot 6: energize stepper phase 3; read or write activates this soft switch. Head movement depends on the phase sequence, not this address alone.

symbols.name: COMMENT_D2_MOTOR_OFF
symbols.comment: Disk II slot 6: Disable the selected drive motor; hardware spin-down is not instantaneous. Access is a control strobe, not a stored byte.

symbols.name: COMMENT_D2_MOTOR_ON
symbols.comment: Disk II slot 6: Enable the selected drive motor; allow spin-up time before reading or writing disk data.

symbols.name: COMMENT_D2_DRIVE1
symbols.comment: Disk II slot 6: Select physical drive 1 (connector 1; emulator drive index 0); shared controller signals now address this drive.

symbols.name: COMMENT_D2_DRIVE2
symbols.comment: Disk II slot 6: Select physical drive 2 (connector 2; emulator drive index 1); shared controller signals now address this drive.

symbols.name: COMMENT_D2_Q6L_DATA
symbols.comment: Disk II slot 6: Set Q6=0: with Q7=0 read the disk data latch (bit 7 marks a complete disk nibble); with Q7=1 shift/write the loaded byte. Current emulator advances its disk byte position here.

symbols.name: COMMENT_D2_Q6H_LOAD
symbols.comment: Disk II slot 6: Set Q6=1: with Q7=0 select write-protect sensing; with Q7=1 load the write-data latch from the CPU bus. STA supplies the outgoing byte; this is not a general RAM register.

symbols.name: COMMENT_D2_Q7L_READ
symbols.comment: Disk II slot 6: Set Q7=0: with Q6=0 select disk read; with Q6=1 select write-protect sense (hardware D7=1 means protected). Current emulator does not expose full hardware write-protect readback.

symbols.name: COMMENT_D2_Q7H_WRITE
symbols.comment: Disk II slot 6: Set Q7=1: with Q6=0 select disk write/shift; with Q6=1 select write-data load. Switching Q7 changes the meaning of the Q6 strobes.

symbols.name: COMMENT_D2_GCR_CAND
symbols.comment: Disk II BOOT0: Test a candidate disk nibble while building the inverse 6-and-2 GCR translation table.

symbols.name: COMMENT_D2_GCR_BITS
symbols.comment: Disk II BOOT0: Shift and test the candidate bit pattern to determine whether it belongs in the GCR decode table.

symbols.name: COMMENT_D2_GCR_NEXT
symbols.comment: Disk II BOOT0: Advance to the next candidate disk nibble; accepted values map to six-bit values in page 3.

symbols.name: COMMENT_D2_SEEK_ZERO
symbols.comment: Disk II BOOT0: Recalibrate the selected drive toward track 0 by cycling stepper phases and allowing mechanical settling time.

symbols.name: COMMENT_D2_READ_SECTOR
symbols.comment: Disk II BOOT0: Sector-read entry; clear carry and scan disk nibbles for an address prologue. Boot parameters use $3D for sector, $41 for track, and $26/$27 for destination.

symbols.name: COMMENT_D2_SCAN_PROLOG
symbols.comment: Disk II BOOT0: Save the address/data search phase in carry before scanning for a prologue; PHP preserves that phase across byte comparisons.

symbols.name: COMMENT_D2_WAIT_D5
symbols.comment: Disk II BOOT0: Poll the disk read latch until bit 7 is set, then look for the first prologue byte $D5.

symbols.name: COMMENT_D2_MATCH_D5
symbols.comment: Disk II BOOT0: Check/recheck a candidate $D5 prologue byte after the polling read.

symbols.name: COMMENT_D2_WAIT_AA
symbols.comment: Disk II BOOT0: Poll for a complete disk nibble and verify the second prologue byte $AA.

symbols.name: COMMENT_D2_WAIT_MARK
symbols.comment: Disk II BOOT0: Read the third prologue byte: $96 identifies an address field; $AD identifies a data field after the requested address was found.

symbols.name: COMMENT_D2_ADDR_START
symbols.comment: Disk II BOOT0: Start decoding the three useful 4-and-4 address-field bytes: volume, track and sector.

symbols.name: COMMENT_D2_ADDR_SAVE
symbols.comment: Disk II BOOT0: Save the previous decoded address value; repeated passes leave the decoded track in $40 and sector in A.

symbols.name: COMMENT_D2_ADDR_ODD
symbols.comment: Disk II BOOT0: Read the first disk nibble of a 4-and-4 encoded address byte; rotate it to prepare the odd data bits.

symbols.name: COMMENT_D2_ADDR_EVEN
symbols.comment: Disk II BOOT0: Read the second address nibble and AND it with the rotated first nibble to reconstruct the address byte.

symbols.name: COMMENT_D2_AUX_START
symbols.comment: Disk II BOOT0: Start reading the 86 auxiliary 6-and-2 values that carry the low two bits of each sector byte.

symbols.name: COMMENT_D2_AUX_INDEX
symbols.comment: Disk II BOOT0: Preserve the descending auxiliary-buffer index in $3C before a disk read overwrites Y.

symbols.name: COMMENT_D2_AUX_READ
symbols.comment: Disk II BOOT0: Poll for a complete disk nibble in Y, translate it through the GCR table, and XOR-decode the auxiliary stream.

symbols.name: COMMENT_D2_MAIN_INDEX
symbols.comment: Disk II BOOT0: Preserve the destination byte index in $3C before reading the next main data nibble.

symbols.name: COMMENT_D2_MAIN_READ
symbols.comment: Disk II BOOT0: Read and GCR/XOR-decode the main six-bit sector data; store it through the destination pointer at $26/$27.

symbols.name: COMMENT_D2_CHECK_READ
symbols.comment: Disk II BOOT0: Read and translate the final checksum nibble; the accumulated XOR should reduce to zero.

symbols.name: COMMENT_D2_CHECKSUM
symbols.comment: Disk II BOOT0: Reject a nonzero checksum and restart sector search; on success proceed to reconstruct the original eight-bit sector bytes.

symbols.name: COMMENT_D2_AUX_RESET
symbols.comment: Disk II BOOT0: Reset the auxiliary-buffer index for distributing the stored low-bit pairs across the 256 sector bytes.

symbols.name: COMMENT_D2_RECOMBINE
symbols.comment: Disk II BOOT0: Recover two low bits from the auxiliary buffer, rotate them into each six-bit byte, and write the reconstructed byte back to the sector buffer.

symbols.name: COMMENT_D2_BOOT0
symbols.comment: Disk II BOOT0: Bootstrap entry and controller signature; build the GCR table, identify the slot, spin up drive 1, seek track 0, and load BOOT1.

symbols.name: COMMENT_D2_FIND_SLOT
symbols.comment: Disk II BOOT0: Call the Monitor RTS at $FF58 and inspect its return-address bytes on the stack to derive slot*16; TSX reads the stack pointer, not the processor status.

symbols.name: COMMENT_D2_INIT_IO
symbols.comment: Disk II BOOT0: Configure Q7 low, Q6 low, drive 1, and motor on using slot-relative $C08x,X operands.

symbols.name: COMMENT_D2_INIT_BUFFER
symbols.comment: Disk II BOOT0: Initialize the sector destination pointer to $0800 and the requested track and sector to zero.

symbols.name: COMMENT_D2_NEXT_SECTOR
symbols.comment: Disk II BOOT0: Advance the requested sector after decoding one page; compare against the sector count in the boot block at $0800.

symbols.name: COMMENT_D2_ENTER_BOOT1
symbols.comment: Disk II BOOT0: Jump to $0801 to execute the next-stage loader; $0800 is its requested-sector count, not a BASIC program header.

notes: All 16 slot-6 controller I/O offsets are named, plus 29 descriptive BOOT0 code-target labels derived from the supplied PROM file.
Names and comments resolve encoded operand addresses. ROM label records name branch/JSR/JMP targets; this operand-address table does not populate the listing lbl column.
Load the PC-scoped DISKII_PROM_ANNOTATED.symbols.json companion for descriptive listing labels, indexed operands and source comments. It retains the original PROM names as aliases.
Indexed slot-relative operands such as $C08C,X are not $C0EC until X=$60 is added. This dataset deliberately does not claim the $C080-$C08F slot-0/language-card addresses as Disk II.
For another slot s, controller base=$C080+$10*s and ROM base=$C000+$100*s. Relocate value, hex, scope and scopeHex consistently.
The Q6/Q7 descriptions identify hardware modes and note relevant simplifications in the current emulator; they do not promise emulation of every electrical side effect.
